la:verb:eiuro.html:
ē-jūro (mostly post-Aug., ,
v.infra, and ējĕro, like pejero, class., Scip. ap. twice; ; ; ; ), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to refuse or reject by oath, to abjure, a t. t. of jurid., polit., and mercant. lang.
In jurid. lang.: forum or judicem iniquum sibi, to reject, refuse on oath a court or a judge, as unjust, Scip. l. l.; l. l.; Manut. and Wernsd.—
In polit. law lang.: magistratum, imperium, etc., to lay down, resign, abdicate an office, at the same time swearing to have administered it according to law: jurando abdicare, ; ; ; ; ; and absol., .—
Transf. beyond the polit. sphere (like abdicare), to abandon, forswear, disown any thing: militiam, to swear one's self unfit for service, cf. III. infra; Plaut. Fragm. ap. Paul. ex Müll.: patriam,; cf.: patriae nomen,; Asin. Pollio ap. : liberos,; cf. patrem (with aversari),.—Poet.: fidem domitoremque inimicum (leo),.—
In mercant. lang.: bonam copiam (as the opp. of jurare bonam copiam), to declare on oath that one has not wherewithal to pay his debts, to swear that one is insolvent, Manut.
